methodology: challenge-assumptions
---

# The clinic's reputation after a bad outcome

Eight months ago a referred patient from one of the three villages died after a complication the family believes the clinic should have caught earlier. Whether that belief is medically accurate is a separate question from its effect, which has been substantial: staff report that referrals from that specific village have dropped noticeably since, and word in the community links the clinic's name to the outcome regardless of what the chart actually shows.

The team's working assumption has been that the drop is temporary and will fade with time, the way these things are assumed to. Nobody has actually tested that assumption against the referral numbers from other clinics that had a comparable incident, and a few staff privately suspect the opposite: that reputational damage in a small, tightly connected community does not decay on its own, it decays only when something visible replaces the story, and right now nothing has replaced it. The team has not agreed on whether that is even the right question to be asking yet.
